emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([pwq->stats[PWQ_STAT_COMPLETED]++ @3244]) from either worker (a single-location non-atomic RMW that assumes no concurrent conflicting access)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@process_one_work:3244 = the peer worker's concurrent pwq->stats[PWQ_STAT_COMPLETED]++ on the same pool_workqueue's slot
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the increment is executed AFTER pool->lock was dropped (between trace_workqueue_execute_end and the later raw_spin_lock_irq(&pool->lock)), so neither worker holds pool->lock at :3244 -> no serialize establishes mutual exclusion on the shared counter
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho = atomic(single-location access) broken by a concurrent unsynchronized RMW from a peer worker -> data race (lost update on the completion counter)

fix_maps_to: patch moves pwq->stats[PWQ_STAT_COMPLETED]++ into the existing pool->lock critical section (after raw_spin_lock_irq(&pool->lock)) -> serialize(pool->lock, [increment]) -> establishes the atomic RMW
recall_risk_notes: Clean self-race on a concrete struct field, with surface support (vulnerability_surface gives primary_object + access_paths for both workers). Both threads enter worker_thread->process_one_work, so a self-race pair must be spawned (standard). Main risk is site-precise protection arbitration: process_one_work DOES take pool->lock elsewhere, but the lock is RELEASED across the work-function call where :3244 sits; the static not_lock_protected check must be precise to the site (lock dropped, then re-acquired) rather than concluding 'function holds pool->lock'. If it wrongly treats :3244 as pool->lock-protected, the bug is missed.
